stemMd: A system absorbs 500 J of heat and does 180 J of work on its surroundings. What is its internal-energy change?
explanationMd: With work done by the system taken as positive, the first law is ΔU=Q−W. Thus ΔU=500−180=320 J, an increase.

distractorRationale.c: This includes only the work and omits absorbed heat.
distractorRationale.d: Work done by the system removes energy rather than adding it.
distractorRationale.e: The absorbed heat exceeds the energy transferred out as work.
